The longer cycles did a great job of washing and drying the dishes. I even put some dishes with dry caked on food (I usually rinse them a bit first) and it did great. Ample room for silverware. The 3rd shelf at the top is a great place to put the microwave turntable plate. Satisfied once I figured out the intricacies of using it. But still disappointed in the shortcomings of the Quick wash cycle. Delivery was timely and went fine. I gave it a 4 because when they took the old washer out as they exited, they left a trail of water from the kitchen to the front door for me to mop up.

Sentence (English): This product in my experience is extremely low quality and low durability.
Comments (English): [ Terrible Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This product in my experience is extremely low quality and low durability. Purchased in 2020 and only having the appliance for 4 years. After about 1 year the carriers for the bottom basket broke in multiple positions due to regular use. I ended up buying replacement parts and not making a big deal out of it. Fast forward to July 2024 I set the dishwasher to run like any other time and left the house. Upon my return home, I found a kitchen flooded in water and the water went underneath my vinyl flooring onto the sub-floor and leaked into my basement. This resulted in the need to rebuild the entire kitchen floor and replace all cabinets around my island. Inspecting the failure cause I found the little elbow hose on the bottom of the dishwasher having a 1 inch hole in it. After I contacted GE customer service to explain my situation I was simply told that someone could come out to repair the dishwasher at my cost! I find this customer support and service unreasonable. Thanks for your product destroying my kitchen and now you want me to pay you to get it fixed! Absolute joke of a product and customer service. I will not seek to purchase another GE product. My point is that I understand appliances don't last forever. I can also understand being responsible for fixing an appliance that is outside of warranty. However, this wasn't just a failure where the appliance wasn't cleaning or the racks were bad. This was literally a giant hole causing the complete water to leak out and destroy personal property.

Sentence (English): The KitchenAid dishwasher was installed about 5 weeks ago.
Comments (English): [ Decent dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The KitchenAid dishwasher was installed about 5 weeks ago. I choose it over the Bosch in the same price range because the racks seemed sturdier and the arrangement of spaces for plates seemed more useful compared to the Bosch. It cleans well. Took a star off because it is definitely noisier than 44 decibels. While running it makes a constant annoying mechanical noise like a microwave running. I avoid running the dishwasher while I need to be in the kitchen, so it is inferior to my previous dishwasher in this respect. Some internet commentators indicated that the noise abates after 6 weeks. It may now be less than at first, but still not at all what was expected from the claimed decibel rating. Interior design: the spacing for plates on the bottom rack is wider than previous dishwashers, so fewer plates fit in, but there is space on the second rack for smaller plates. Also on the second rack, cereal bowls fit in perfectly, better than previous dishwashers. In general, I can fit a usual load of dishes in. I kept the silverware bins from the old dishwasher rather than using the long large, deep rack that came with the KitchenAid. The items that are difficult to arrange are small Pyrex food containers, their small lids, and similarly small plates and saucers. The wide spacing of the tines on the racks makes it difficult to load small items and the special area on the third rack doesn't hold enough for my needs. The area in the third rack for glasses and mugs is good for those items that fit and the special spray rod does a good job of cleaning them. Another aspect that was attractive is the leak detector. Our previous dishwasher leaked enough to ruin kitchen cabinets before it was noticed.

The door, inconveniently, doesn't crack open to help, it has to be wide open. Being very busy this summer, Best Buy's return window opened and closed almost immediately. What was that, two weeks? So here we are, stuck with a wildly overpriced and wildly underperforming appliance. Choose any product other than this, believe me. Terrible.

Positives are that you can make a lot of adjustments in the rack to fit larger items and the silverware tray holds a great volume. Also the ability to receive an alert through the app when the machine is done is pretty convenient.

Sentence (English): This is the first dishwasher I've ever owned, but I am impressed with it.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This is the first dishwasher I've ever owned, but I am impressed with it. For one the machine as a whole is beautiful, I love the stainless everything from the outside to the inside and after you open it post running a load that baby sparkles. I am also pleased with its cleaning ability I use it with Finish quantum pods and the rinse aid. The water here is slightly hard so I do get a few items with spots after a cycle that's why I wish my machine had a compartment for dish salts so I could prevent that. I've adjusted the settings on it( which are hard to locate and somewhat difficult to program) and I still get spots. However dishes are clean and rarely still wet(only Tupperware and plastics) I am also pretty displeased with the length of the cycles, the auto cycle which I use most of the time is 2hr 10min so I usually have to wait until night to run it so it doesn't affect my water pressure if I'm tying to shower or use the sink. The quickest setting is about 35 mins I believe for a half load, not sure why there's such a big time difference for a half vs a full but anyhow I am pleased with the dishwasher overall and those few grievances are negligible compared to life without having a machine at all.

Sentence (English): Dishwasher is probably a 4.5, realistically.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher Great, Delivery/Replacement/Install not ] || ---------------- || Dishwasher is probably a 4.5, realistically. But the entire experience was troublesome. I made sure to go through the 1 star reviews of quiet a few dishwashers, the consensus on those were overwhelmingly the same experience I had, was just hoping it was the "vocal minority", but turns out it was actually a common problem. I want to give a 1-star, just so this is more visible, but hopefully people sort by "most recent". Bought this July 9th, along with 2 other major appliances. All items delivered on July 13th, though dishwasher had a separate install date, which I was aware of, so I had the unit dropped off in the living room. Installers show up on July 16th, ready to go. They locate water shutoff and get their gear down to pull the old unit out. They open up the new dishwasher, still in its box and let me know the front is dented. There are also 2 dents on the rear corner of the tub (which is stainless steel). They packed up their things, packed up the dishwasher, said they were taking it back to the warehouse and I should be getting a call in about 2 minutes, then left. Didn't hear a word about it until July 18th, which was someone confirming an install the next day between 9am and 2pm--So I had to cancel plans. July 19th, different installers show up and get their gear in and get ready to remove existing unit when one guy asks "You have the dishwasher, right? ". Nope, thought they had it, since I had no communication from Costco or guys who took the damaged unit. They pack up, I'm talking to the installer, explaining what happened, he was nice enough to call Costco and Costco called me about 2 minutes later and set up the replacement and install for July 23rd. July 23rd comes and the 3rd pair of installers show up. They DO have the dishwasher. They unpack it outside. Everything look good. They bring it in and get ready to remove the old unit, which is about as far as this story goes. I'm told it will be an extra $150 because its not a "basic Install". He was also trying to have me replace my airgap, citing "there is usually problems with them", I told him I hadn't had issues with it. Then I told him I'd do it myself. I asked if they were still taking the old unit away, he said no, they only get paid to install it. But he assured me Costco will refund the "install fee" and come pick up my old unit for free. Unsure if that's true, since after looking at the customer service section, its stated that an alternate haul away incurs a fee, paid by the member. Saw nothing about a refund for "self install". What's more bothersome is the previous 2 installers got to the same point Either way, I did install myself. I paid $20 for a 12ft drain hose, which I taped to the old one and pulled through. Also bought a 10ft supply like for about $30, taped that to the old one and pulled through. I would have been perfectly fine paying $50 for the parts. Labor was really no more work than a "basic" install. But at least I'm confident in my ability to install a dishwasher properly. Guidelines don't mention anything about mentioning install issues. And, against my better judgement after reading countless install headaches on various dishwashers, I went ahead and did it. I'll save myself the trouble in the future and just grab something on clearance and install it myself.

They locate water shutoff and get their gear down to pull the old unit out. They open up the new dishwasher, still in its box and let me know the front is dented. There are also 2 dents on the rear corner of the tub (which is stainless steel). They packed up their things, packed up the dishwasher, said they were taking it back to the warehouse and I should be getting a call in about 2 minutes, then left. Didn't hear a word about it until July 18th, which was someone confirming an install the next day between 9am and 2pm--So I had to cancel plans. July 19th, different installers show up and get their gear in and get ready to remove existing unit when one guy asks "You have the dishwasher, right? ". They pack up, I'm talking to the installer, explaining what happened, he was nice enough to call Costco and Costco called me about 2 minutes later and set up the replacement and install for July 23rd. They bring it in and get ready to remove the old unit, which is about as far as this story goes. I'm told it will be an extra $150 because its not a "basic Install". He was also trying to have me replace my airgap, citing "there is usually problems with them", I told him I hadn't had issues with it. Then I told him I'd do it myself. I asked if they were still taking the old unit away, he said no, they only get paid to install it. But he assured me Costco will refund the "install fee" and come pick up my old unit for free. Unsure if that's true, since after looking at the customer service section, its stated that an alternate haul away incurs a fee, paid by the member. Saw nothing about a refund for "self install". What's more bothersome is the previous 2 installers got to the same point Either way, I did install myself. I paid $20 for a 12ft drain hose, which I taped to the old one and pulled through. Also bought a 10ft supply like for about $30, taped that to the old one and pulled through. I would have been perfectly fine paying $50 for the parts. Labor was really no more work than a "basic" install. But at least I'm confident in my ability to install a dishwasher properly. Guidelines don't mention anything about mentioning install issues. I'll save myself the trouble in the future and just grab something on clearance and install it myself.

Sentence (English): After our house flooded with Hurricane Harvey the one thing I was excited about ordering were new appliances.
Comments (English): [ Sad day in our kitchen ] || ---------------- || After our house flooded with Hurricane Harvey the one thing I was excited about ordering were new appliances. I love the styling, features, and quality of KitchenAid products and was thrilled to purchase the 25.8 Cu. Ft. French Door refrigerator (KRMF706ESS), the beautiful dishwasher with a 3rd rack (KDTE304GPS), the 30" Double Oven with convection (KODE500ESS), and an enormous Microwave with a removable shelf for lots of options (KNHP519ESS) which had a special cherry cabinet built around it. Our kitchen was finally ready, just in time for Christmas 2018.The refrigerator was the first to have issues, with the ice maker leaking, stopping, freezing the entire thing up which had to be thawed with a hair dryer. We replaced the ice container 6/20, motor, seal and shaft 8/20, I/M leaking and stopped cooling on both sides 6/22. In August 2023 the entire fridge had quit working correctly and would have cost over 1K for parts which 'might' have solved the issue.Sadly our wonderful microwave started making a loud noise and quit running October 2023 and the technician gave us the news that the Magnetron shorted, and couldn't be fixed. We have a whole house surge protector so we know it wasn't caused by electrical issues.Now in the summer of 2024 our dishwasher quit working correctly. The motor has died in the main wash assembly. It would cost more than $600 as the entire bottom of the unit must be replaced.Since 3 of our 4 expensive KitchenAid appliances have failed I asked the technician about our very pricy oven which he warned us that if the heating element on the bottom goes out, the removal and repair for it will be astronomical, because of the way it is constructed.I absolutely love these appliances, they were all top notch and had every feature I could ever want, but I can't believe that I have spent over $10,000 and am having to replace 3 of the 4 in less than 6 years!

It's intuitive and simple to use. Just pour in water, select a setting, and press the button to start washing. While it doesn't have as many features as a large dishwasher, it's a solid performer, and as a single-person household, it's incredibly useful. 2. Since there's no plumbing involved, it's easy to use regardless of whether you live in a rented or leased house. Just pack the accessories and take them with you when you move! This is why I bought it without hesitation. 3. Self-installation is incredibly easy! However, the instructions and video mention connecting a hose at the back. This is a bit of a simplification! I hope they'll address that. 4. It has excellent cleaning power. It cleans well unless it's overly sticky or greasy. * However, it didn't clean my non-smooth plastic containers. I had to scrub the surface with a sponge to remove any remaining stains. **It cleaned wine glasses well, but it didn't remove any lip stains from eating with greasy food. There were also some water stains. # Tip: I don't know if it's because the weather has been hot lately or what, but the inside of the dishwasher was still damp for a long time after I finished washing and even the next day. Since I only use it 2-3 times a week anyway, I unplugged it, left the door open for a while, and let the inside dry until all the moisture was gone before closing the door. As a result, I'm using it very conveniently. It's the perfect dishwasher for a 1-2 person household. I invested around 300,000 won and it saved me a lot of time and improved my quality of life. I recommend it.

It's intuitive and simple to use. Just pour in water, select a setting, and press the button to start washing. While it doesn't have as many features as a large dishwasher, it's a solid performer, and as a single-person household, it's incredibly useful. 2. Since there's no plumbing involved, it's easy to use regardless of whether you live in a rented or leased house. Just pack the accessories and take them with you when you move! This is why I bought it without hesitation. 3. Self-installation is incredibly easy! However, the instructions and video mention connecting a hose at the back. This is a bit of a simplification! I hope they'll address that. 4. It has excellent cleaning power. It cleans well unless it's overly sticky or greasy. * However, it didn't clean my non-smooth plastic containers. I had to scrub the surface with a sponge to remove any remaining stains. **It cleaned wine glasses well, but it didn't remove any lip stains from eating with greasy food. Since I only use it 2-3 times a week anyway, I unplugged it, left the door open for a while, and let the inside dry until all the moisture was gone before closing the door. As a result, I'm using it very conveniently. It's the perfect dishwasher for a 1-2 person household. I invested around 300,000 won and it saved me a lot of time and improved my quality of life. I recommend it.

I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. Comments (English): [ I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been thinking about it for a while. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. Comments (English): [ I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been thinking about it for a while. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent.
