I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to wash everything, including dishes and cooking utensils, but space constraints mean I'm only going to use dishes and cutlery. ] || ---------------- || I live alone. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses. After filling the dishwasher, your hands will be wet, and since dishwasher detergent dissolves well in water, you need to dry your hands thoroughly before using the detergent. I'd love to use a dishwasher, but my kitchen is so small that I've been debating for quite some time. I'd love to wash everything, even dishes and utensils, but space constraints mean I'd rather just use dishes and cutlery. After browsing a few brands of mini dishwashers, I finally bought one! ^^ I chose the Minix because of its compact water supply system, its visible interior, the automatic door-opening feature after washing, and its design. :) <Packaging & Delivery>. The dishwasher and the complimentary detergent were shipped separately, but they arrived together. The box itself wasn't as heavy as I thought! The box itself had a string attached, but it wasn't just there for easy lifting. The packaging was thoughtful: cutting the string allowed the box lid to open, making it easy to remove the dishwasher. The inside of the box was meticulously secured, ensuring no damage during shipping. <Installation>. - Before installation, I opened the water tank at the bottom, and it was easy to open if I wanted to clean it during use. - The product itself wasn't as heavy as I thought, so I had no trouble lifting it by myself. However, when I placed the product on the water tank and tried to connect the drain/water supply, the narrow space made it difficult to connect the drain/water supply pipes on the back of the product. I think it would be easier to connect the drain/water supply pipes to the back of the product first, and then rotate the product to install it! - There's a black cardboard(?) inside the product that holds the tray and other items in place, but at first, it wouldn't come off. I struggled for a while, moving the tray and tilting the cardboard. If you look closely at the picture, the cardboard got caught on the wings at the top of the dishwasher when they were horizontal. If you place the top wings vertically so that the wings can pass through the holes in the cardboard, it will come off easily! <Washing and drying>. - After installation, use is very simple. First, turn on the power, open the drip tray at the front of the water tank, and fill it with water. Thanks to the protrusions inside the drip tray, I was amazed that even when I turned on the water, not a single drop splashed out! However, sink faucets usually use both a single-stream mode and a shower mode. In shower mode, water would splash. When I turn it on in single-stream mode, even if I turn on the sink water really hard, it doesn't splash at all. - There are several washing modes, but I started with the standard mode first. The time is listed as 1 hour, which is the washing time. The drying time after that seems to vary depending on the environment. When I first used it, I was confused because the dishwasher made a noise for almost 3 minutes until the 1 hour timer went down to 57 minutes, but there was no movement inside the glass. I thought I had installed it wrong, so I looked around for a while and it seems that the first 2-3 minutes are when the water in the water tank is sucked into the main unit, so it's only a sound. The same thing happens when I drain the water that was being washed and then supply new water. - The initial water sucking sound seems to be the loudest, and there's almost no noise during the wash. The water sucking sound seems quieter than that of a washing machine. When the door is closed, the sound isn't really audible inside the room. - After the 1-hour washing cycle is over, the door automatically opens to release heat and moisture, then closes and the fan runs, repeating this process to dry. Since steam and heat are released when the door is opened, you should always keep the area around it clean. <Washing Results, Pros and Cons>. - I haven't used it many times yet, but there were some white spots left after drying. Are they water marks? Not detergent residue? Other than that, it seems to have washed very well. I always wash the dishes with slightly warm water, but the weather has been so hot and humid lately that doing dishes in the kitchen has become a real burden. I'm satisfied that this mini dishwasher has helped ease that burden to some extent! - It cleans the spoons and chopsticks well, but I feel like they shouldn't overlap, so I have to place them one by one, even the chopsticks, which feels a bit cumbersome. I want to put it upright in the cutlery holder, but since it's a mini dishwasher, I need to find a cutlery holder that fits in the tray compartment and where the chopsticks won't fall out, which means less space, so I'm a little worried~. - It seems to have the most space on the second floor among mini dishwashers. It's long enough to put cooking utensils other than cutlery, which is nice. <Special detergent, all-in-one tablet>. - It says it's apple mint scented, but honestly, I'm not sure about the scent~ But it's convenient because it's tailored to the size of the Minix dishwasher and the amount of water it uses.
